correctness.rationale: For n>=2, one 1<t<=2 weighted cross edge of K_(n,n,n) changes only the mutual distance of its endpoints; 2^p for within-part distances, 1 for other cross edges. Reconstructed D_p=a(J-I)+(1-a)B0+(b-1)E. Compression to 1-perp and the A/B exchange symmetry yields symmetric-sector generalized eigenvalue root T_n(eta)>n and antisymmetric Rayleigh bound <n for eta>0, leaving one simple critical mode. Negative-type inheritance and a positive-to-negative critical test produce a unique endpoint strictly below p0=log2(n/(n-1)); Schoenberg ranks give dimensions 3n-1 below, 3n-2 at endpoint vs 3n-3 intact. Expanding the exact quadratic for delta_n=T_n-n gives n delta_n ->eta/3 uniformly eta in [0,1], hence n^3(p0-wp_n(t))->log(t)/(3 log(2)^2). Independent full zero-sum compressed adjacency eigenvalue calculations for n=2,3,5,10 at nontrivial eta agree with T_n to floating precision (<=2e-15). They corroborate, not replace, spectral proof.

originality.rationale: Graph-join QEC theory covers unweighted graph distances and may encompass t=2 edge deletion; that endpoint is not asserted separately new. General negative-type inheritance and multipartite QEC results also supply prior machinery. The assessed contribution is the continuous stretched-edge family 1<t<2 with exact sharp p-threshold, unique equality mode, and cubic derivative scale. These do not logically follow by substituting a weighted edge into the cited unweighted graph-join theorems. Uninspected broader finite-metric rank-one perturbation results remain a risk.
